title: Find the limit before the geometric stop
chapter: §6.3, §6.6 — effectiveness, usable authority and nonlinear limits
brief: Distinguish local effectiveness, usable travel, and nonlinear authority. This explicitly synthetic extension prevents a geometric stop from being mistaken for model validity.
supplied: Does a local slope establish the required ΔCm=-0.25 at a demanded 13.64° elevator deflection?
Straight-line estimate ΔCm=-1.05*deltaDeg*pi/180. For this additional synthetic dataset, the documented local-fit interval is -10 to +10 deg; usable travel reaches +18 deg.
Synthetic extension of the chapter exercise: deltaDeg [-10,0,10,15,18]; observed ΔCm [0.183260,0,-0.183260,-0.20,-0.21]. These are teaching observations, not aircraft test data.
Straight-line estimate, supplied nonlinear observation, local-fit validity and authority conclusion.
The -1.05 per-radian slope is local. Reaching a travel stop does not establish flow attachment, actuator holding ability or rate capability.
At large positive deflection the straight-line estimate overstates the magnitude in this synthetic dataset.
Linear estimate at 18°=-0.329867, but supplied synthetic response=-0.21, short of the -0.25 demand.
Check fit endpoints ±10°; 13.64° lies outside this local straight-line model; maximum supplied negative response magnitude is only 0.21.
Label extrapolation separately from the supplied nonlinear observations; never present the geometric limit as a validated fit boundary.
Plot the tangent and the five supplied observations against deflection. Evaluate the requested deflection against the documented ±10° fit interval.
The local straight-line model cannot establish the requested response; the supplied nonlinear example is insufficient at the declared usable limit.

sweep.units: Elevator deflection in deg; signed pitching-moment increment dimensionless.

experience.scenario: The straight-line elevator model is supported only between −10° and +10°, although the elevator can move to +18°. A requested response gives a calculated angle of 13.64°. This mission asks whether that prediction can be trusted outside the supported range.
experience.task: Enter the supported model range. Decide whether it includes 13.64°, then compare the supplied nonlinear example data with the requested coefficient change of −0.25.
experience.method: The elevator can move farther than the range supported by the straight-line model. Compare each angle with −10° to +10°. Then compare the supplied response data with the requested −0.25 coefficient change. More negative means a stronger nose-down moment. No response measurement is supplied at 13.64°, so do not invent one.
experience.investigate: Inspect 10°, the requested 13.64°, and 18°. Record model qualification separately from the nonlinear evidence and demand.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.

reflection.included: The experiment compares a declared valid range with supplied nonlinear response evidence and the geometric travel stop.
reflection.omitted: Those example data do not establish the response at every aircraft condition or beyond the measured range.
reflection.question: What evidence would justify extending the usable deflection range beyond the range currently supported?
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

experience.terms: A local fit is a straight-line model supported over a stated angle range. Extrapolation means using it outside that range. A travel stop only limits movement. The nonlinear example data can curve away from the straight line.
